methodology: Precision cannot be judged against a hand-labeled ground truth for all ~430 predicted delta items in the time available, so it is estimated from a fixed-seed (random.seed(42)) stratified random sample: 20 of 'modified', 12 of 'removed', all of 'added' at the time of labeling. Each sampled item was manually checked against the two source PDFs' extracted text (see conversation / data/samples) and judged correct (a real, correctly-paired difference) or incorrect (either a PDF line-segmentation/kerning artifact reported as if it were a content change, or a genuine cross-alignment error pairing two unrelated fragments).
generated_with: random.seed(42); random.sample(by_change_type['modified'], 20); random.sample(by_change_type['removed'], 12); by_change_type['added'] (all, 11 at labeling time)

known_failure_categories: Note-number prefix fragmentation: enumerated notes (e.g. '11. COMPRESSOR MOTOR...') sometimes split the leading 'N.' token into its own text fragment in one PDF export but not the other, due to kerning/line-break differences at export time. This is the single largest source of false positives (~7 of 12 sampled errors).

Cross-alignment in dense/generic regions: when many short, similarly-positioned text fragments cluster (trailing words of adjacent notes, the fitting/valve-code legend grid), the position+text blended score can pair the wrong two fragments together, reporting a 'modified' item between two unrelated pieces of text.
Kerning/glyph-spacing artifacts: punctuation-adjacent tokens like 'FB/ILO' vs 'FB ILO' can extract as different line groupings between two PDF exports of the same template.
